unit.why: A homiletic anthology passage on heavenly decrees that quotes several sources; it includes two short narratives about R. Elimelekh of Lizhensk: one in which he answers from the World of Truth, and one in which he cries out and sees the Maggid of Mezritch.
unit.boundary_note: part of a running thematic anthology ('מענין גזירה') that begins in the previous division and continues into the next; the opening Kozhenits saying and the closing Zusha remark are teachings, not stories

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ ש"צ וירא וז״ל ע״ד ששמעתי
stories.summary_en: After R. Elimelekh's death, when a decree fell, all Israel looked to him for help; he answered from the World of Truth that he knows the reason for the decree and even agrees to it, so he cannot pray against it, and they must look to a living tsaddik who does not know its reason.

quotes: והשיב אני מעלמא דקשוט וכל רז לא אניש לי
tags.why: the deceased tsaddik answers the living

quotes: יש לכם לחלות עיניכם בהצדיק ההוא
tags.why: the tsaddik's power to intercede against decrees

quotes: זה יכול לצעוק ולהתפלל אולי יענה בתפלתו
אני מעלמא דקשוט וכל רז לא אניש לי
tags.why: he speaks from the World of Truth

quotes: בגוירה וכו׳ תלו כל ישראל ביניהם בו
tags.why: protection of the community from a decree is sought
an anecdote embedded in a homiletic discussion of decrees

stories.summary_en: R. Elimelekh cried out bitterly over a great calamity, saw his late master the Maggid of Mezritch, and asked why the Maggid was silent; the Maggid replied that in heaven they see only good, so those on earth must strive in prayer to annul the evil.

quotes: והיה רואה אז ביראה את עורו הה״ק המגיד
והיה צועק אליו למה אתם מחשים לעת צרה כזאת
והשיב כי בשנים אין אנו רואים שום רע

tags.why: disciple appeals to his late master

quotes: כי בשנים אין אנו רואים שום רע רק הטוב והחסד
ואבותינו ספרו לנו ממרן אא״ז הה״ק
tags.why: framed as a family tradition handed down
